newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW-Malaysia's TA Bank eyes S.Africa listing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Malaysia's TA Bank eyes S.Africa listing.

text.p: TA Bank South Africa, a subsidiary of Malaysia's TA Enterprise Berhad, said on Wednesday it planned to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange within the next five years.

The bank opened its first African operation in Johannesburg on Wednesday with a capital base of 150 million rand -- an amount managing director Henry Shaw said the company had the capacity to triple by the next decade.
"We expect to increase our capital base to 500 million rand over the next four to five years," Shaw told Reuters in an interview.
"Capital will be provided from Malaysia and in that period, if not sooner, we aim to list the group's activities in South Africa," he said.
The bank, which is the third firm in the TA group to set up shop in South Africa after TA Securities' and TA Properties' launches last year, aims to cater for the mid-range corporate market.
It will offer a limited range of products such as term loans, leases, instalment sales, deposits and foreign exchange.
"We will be providing some services to the top end of the retail market where synergies exist between TA Securities and ourselves," Shaw said.

Datuk Tony Tiah, TA Enterprise executive chairman, said the the company had set up operations in South Africa because the country was emerging as a regional centre for investment and economic growth in southern Africa.
"With TA Bank, we will now be able to play a more complete role as a financial group offering a wide spectrum of financial service not only in South Africa but across our entire network," he said.
Shaw said the bank was currently reviewing its options in neighbouring southern African countries with a view to setting up other banks in the region.
TA Bank South Africa would also act as a conduit for investment and trade between South Africa and South East Asia, Shaw added.
TA Enterprise Berhad is one of Malaysia's leading financial houses with operations in Australia, India, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Hong Kong and the Philippines.
